reference_answer: In the United States, nearly all workers must pay Social Security and Medicare taxes, also known as payroll taxes or FICA. It's important to understand that these taxes are not savings plans, and the money you pay is not explicitly allocated to an account in your name. Instead, it funds the benefits received by current retirees and beneficiaries. When you retire, your benefits will be financed by the contributions of the still-employed workers paying these taxes. It's worth noting that FICA taxes are separate from federal and state income taxes, and as a sole proprietor, you are responsible for both types of taxes. Furthermore, there's a distinction between FICA taxes when you are an employee and when you are self-employed. Typically, FICA taxes are divided equally between the employer and the employee, with each paying half. However, if you are self-employed, you are responsible for paying both halves. This is commonly known as the self-employment tax. You may be receiving benefits, but you are also still working, so you still have to pay the tax.

You can only deduct  what something cost  even if you had done volunteer work for a charity as a sole prop you could only deduct your actual costs. If you paid an employee to do charity work or to learn something related to the business that would be deductible as a normal business expense. It would be impossible for the IRS to determine the value of your time and it would open the tax system to an enormous amount of fraud (think of being able to make up time spent or writing off time spent volunteering at a soup kitchen or any other charity). Nevertheless, you can write off expenses you have involved in doing the work, equipment and supplies used to do the work along with any wages you paid an employee or contractor to do said work.
In other words, charitable donations, capital expenses or my time could be make my taxesa lower, right?

There are some tax-deductible options related to charitable activities. However, it's important to clarify that you cannot deduct the value of your time or services, including the income lost while working as an unpaid volunteer for a qualified organization. This includes charitable donations of time or services. However, you can deduct actual costs associated with volunteering, such as expenses for equipment, supplies, or wages paid to employees or contractors for work related to the charity. If you have donated items like a published book that you authored (not specifically written for the organization), you might be able to deduct its fair market value. In summary, while you cannot directly deduct the value of your time or services, you can deduct certain expenses related to charitable activities, which may help lower your tax burden. question: how does pre-market trading work?
reference_answer: Pre-market trading takes place before the regular trading hours (RTH) of the stock market. For example, pre-market hours are from 4:00 a.m. to 9:30 a.m. Eastern Time (ET) on the NASDAQ stock market. During pre-market hours, you can place limit orders, but you cannot place market orders due to lower liquidity. This is because the volume and liquidity are generally much lower during pre-market hours compared to RTH. If an unexpected world event occurs, the volume and liquidity might increase. It is important to note that not all brokers allow pre-market trading, and if they do, you might need to specify that you want your order to be executed during pre-market hours.

Creating a single global market would be quite complex and challenging for several reasons. First, each country has its own exchange, which is closely tied to its local currency. Exchanges primarily support transactions and settlements in their local currency, and securities are denominated in a single currency. Cross-currency translation would complicate the trading process, as it would require additional steps and considerations.
Furthermore, citizens and businesses in most countries are restricted to having bank accounts in local currency, making it difficult or impossible to open a domestic bank account in a foreign-denominated currency. A public company headquartered in a given country is more likely to do business with local citizenry and businesses in that currency, and thus look for investors from the same pool, which generally means listing in local currency on an exchange in that country.

question: Using credit card points to pay for tax deductible business expenses
reference_answer: When using credit card points to pay for tax-deductible business expenses, the expenses are not actually deductible because the points used effectively cancel out the cost. However, if the points were earned on a personal credit card and used for business-related expenses, the employer can reimburse the employee for those expenses, and it seems the IRS follows an unofficial "don't ask, don't tell" rule regarding any rewards or cashback earned on the employee's personal card. It's important to note that credit card fees for personal expenses are not tax-deductible, while fees for business credit cards are deductible on Schedule C or the appropriate form for reporting business income and expenses. If you have a card used for both business and personal expenses, it's advisable to get separate cards for clarity and ease of accounting. In summary, while the expenses themselves may not be deductible when using credit card points, the employer can reimburse the employee for the expenses, and having separate cards for business and personal use is recommended, i.e., getting a personal card that you only use for business expenses,  if you don't opt for a business card. It makes it very clear that expenses on that card are business expenses, and is just more professional.

question: In the US, does getting a loan with a cosigner, help your credit rating?
reference_answer: In the US getting a loan with a cosigner, it can potentially help your credit rating, but it depends on how the loan is structured and reported. However a loan with a cosigner can bring a lot problems. In the first scenario, if the loan company reports the status to a credit reporting agency on behalf of both the initiating borrower and the cosigner, then both individuals get a new account on their credit report. Initially, this might decrease related credit scores slightly due to a hard pull, new account with zero history, and increased debt. However, over time, it can have a positive effect on both people's credit ratings if the loan is paid properly. Conversely, if the loan is not paid properly, it will negatively affect both people's credit. In the second scenario, if the loan company only reports to a credit agency on one of you (probably the cosigner), leaving the other as just a backup, it will have no effect on the borrower's credit. In the third scenario, if the loan company doesn't report the loan at all to a credit agency, there will be no direct impact on the borrower's credit. However, if the loan goes into collections and is reported as such, it would negatively affect the borrower's credit. Nevertheless a cosigner will make sure you are going to make every single payment on time because otherwise he will be responsible to pay it  .

question: What's the difference between Market Cap and NAV?
reference_answer: Market capitalization, or Market Cap, is calculated by multiplying the share price by the number of shares. It represents the current market perception of the company's worth. On the other hand, NAV, or net asset value, is the value of the company's stock divided by the number of shares, also known as the book value. NAV reflects the value of the company's assets if it were to sell everything, pay off its debts, and shut down. While Market Cap represents current market sentiment and future expectations, NAV provides a measure of the company's tangible asset value per share. These two values often differ significantly, especially for companies expected to grow or those with substantial intangible assets. NAV is a measurable value, derived from known factors, while Market Cap is determined by the stock price, which is influenced not only by NAV but also by future expectations.

As your company grows, you tend to add people in "layers." The top layer is the first founder or founder. There may be one, two, three, or more of you, but you all start working at about the same time, and you all take the same risk: quitting your jobs to work for a new and unproven company. 
The second layer is the first actual employees. By the time you hire this layer, you've got cash coming in from somewhere (investors or customers—doesn't matter). These people didn't take as much risk because they got a salary from day one, and honestly, they didn't start the company, they joined it as a job. The third layer consists of later employees. By the time they joined the company, it was going pretty well. Each "layer" will be approximately one year for many companies. When your company is big enough to sell to Google or go public, you probably have about six layers: the founders and roughly five layers of employees. Each successive layer is more significant. It's very important to keep your employees happy and ensure they feel part of something other than a job. Make them feel like they're part of a family and support system.

If you lack the time or interest to manage your investments, hiring a financial advisor is a good idea. It's generally better to work with an advisor who charges an annual fee based on a percentage of your account value rather than one who gets paid based on transactions. Here are some tips for starting your own business:
1. Start small and grow it up. You can start online with a website and dedicate an hour a day to researching and planning.
2. Get your family involved 
3. Look for incubators in your area that can provide mentorship and seed money to promising startups.
4. Consider crowdfunding as an alternative financing method.
5. When raising money, be prepared to answer questions about your business strategy and what you will do with the funds to generate profits in the future.
6. Be aware that most startups fail, but also keep in mind that many successful businesses were started by people who were willing to take the risk.
7. Develop forward and backward linkages with the help of startup advisors who can provide expertise and guidance in different verticals of the economy.
8. Be persistent in presenting your business plan to potential investors, but avoid overwhelming them with continuous bombardment.
9. Get business mentors and startup advisors
10. Hire a tax advisor regarding startup costs
Consider reading "The $100 Startup" by Chris Guillebeau and "The 4 Hour Workweek" by Timothy Ferriss for helpful guidance.

This theory states that misappropriating confidential information for securities trading purposes, in breach of a duty owed to the source of that information, requires disclosure or abstention. It's possible to commit normal fraud all day long, and the SEC won't lift a finger, but as soon as you get within a hundred miles of an insider trading deal, they'll come down on you like a ton of bricks. It's an easy case to prove; there is no question about its illegality (even the janitor is expected to take a class on it), and the SEC was specifically set up to stop it after the Great Depression.

The five factors that have a major impact on your FICO credit score are:
1. Payment history: Late payments can negatively affect your score, while on-time payments can improve it.
2. Credit utilization: This refers to how much of your available credit you are currently using. Lower is better, but having 0% usage is not ideal either. Aiming for 10% or less is a good goal.
3. Credit history: This is based on the average age of all your accounts, including credit cards and loans. Older accounts are generally better for your score.
4. Credit mix: Having a diverse mix of credit types (e.g., credit cards, mortgages, auto loans) can positively impact your score.
5. New credit: Applying for new credit can result in a temporary decrease in your score due to the credit inquiries made during the application process. These inquiries remain on your report for two years.
It is important to note that errors and fraud can also impact your credit score, so regularly reviewing your credit reports from the three major credit bureaus (Experian, Equifax, and TransUnion) is recommended.

retrieval_query: How to read bond yield quotes? What do the time, coupon, price, yield, and time mean?
question: How to read bond yield quotes? What do the time, coupon, price, yield, and time mean?
reference_answer:
Bond yield quotes provide important information about a bond's yield, which is the annualized return on investment for the bond. Here's how to read bond yield quotes:
* Time: This refers to the time of the quote presented and indicates when the quote was generated.
* Coupon (coupon rate): This is the amount of interest paid on the bond each period, as specified on the coupon itself. It is usually expressed as a percentage of the bond's face value.
* Price: This is the normalised price of the bond, representing the price of taking a position of $100 worth of the principal in the bond. It is often expressed as a percentage of the bond's face value.
* Yield: This is the interest rate that you would receive by buying at the current price. It is the inverse of the price and represents the annualized return on investment for the bond.
To summarize, when reading bond yield quotes, the time refers to the quote's generation time, while the coupon, price, and yield provide information about the bond's interest payments, market value, and annualized return on investment, respectively.

reference_answer: A stock is an ownership interest in a company, when you buy stocks, you become a partial owner of the company.   A company issues a number of shares you can buy. You buy bonds in a company to lend the company money at an interest rate specified in the bond because you believe the company will be able to repay the debt per the terms of the bond. Think of bonds as kind of like a corporate credit card. When a company needs a lot of cash, it will sell bonds. Bonds tend to be a safer investment than stocks, but offer less potential return.

question: Following an investment guru a good idea?
reference_answer: Following an investment guru can be a good idea if you can afford the time and are looking for more in-depth, fun investment tips. However, it's crucial to understand what you're investing in, including the company's products, and to buy stock in good companies at good prices, considering factors like price to earnings, price to revenue, and price to book. Therefore, while following an investment guru can provide valuable insights, it's essential to conduct your own research and make informed decisions based on your understanding and investment goals. Blindly following other investors, including big investors or gurus, is not recommended, as their strategies may differ from yours. Instead, consider finding someone with similar goals to help guide your investment decisions.

However, it's crucial to understand what you're investing in, including the company's products, and to buy stock in good companies at good prices, considering factors like price to earnings, price to revenue, and price to book. Therefore, while following an investment guru can provide valuable insights, it's essential to conduct your own research and make informed decisions based on your understanding and investment goals. Blindly following other investors, including big investors or gurus, is not recommended, as their strategies may differ from yours. Instead, consider finding someone with similar goals to help guide your investment decisions.
name a few gurus

I don't have a lot of information about individual investment gurus to recommend, but a classic investing guru is Benjamin Graham.  Also Warren Buffett, the CEO of Berkshire Hathaway, is certainly one, who looks for value and ignores hype, greed, and fear.  The websites like Gurufocus (<http://gurufocus.com>) may provide resources for fundamental analysis of "Intelligent Investor" style businesses which can help you identify potential investment gurus.
Those gurus average return?

I don't have specific information on the average returns of investment gurus. However, Warren Buffet, arguably the most successful investor ever lived, has averaged returns of around 21% throughout his 40 years in business.
any online self-help?

Yes, for self-service type online customers, some recommended include OptionsXpress, Marketclub.com, where you can watch and learn from experienced traders like Adam Hewison, and Corey Rosenblum's blog at blog.afraidtotrade.com that offers valuable content focusing on market internals and short-term trades. Trending123.com, run by successful trader John Lansing, provides a live daily chat room for learning from large account day traders. Additionally, seekingalpha.com gives a quick overview and offers free articles on portfolio allocation, and WorldCap which is a mobile solution to analyze global stocks at FactSet and S&P CapitalIQ. Further, YouTube channels and Google searches can help you learn about various aspects of technical analysis and trading strategies.   Remember that no matter how much you learn from others, conducting your own research and making informed decisions based on your understanding and investment goals is crucial.
I meant not online trading.. but training, right?

For self-help in terms of investment training, there are several online resources available. Try online workshops that are relatively cheap but give you a glimpse of a particular subject: Shaw Academy, Udemy, Khan Academy, Investopedia, etc..  For a more hands-on approach, you might consider opening a paper trading account with a brokerage like ThinkOrSwim by TDAmeritrade, which allows you to practice trading without risking real money. Additionally, joining investment clubs or groups in your community can provide opportunities for learning from experienced investors and discussing investment ideas with like-minded individuals.
Is there a minimum amount required?

The minimum amount required for investing in mutual funds, including index funds, typically ranges from a few hundred to a few thousand dollars. For example, a common minimum investment is $3000 for a taxable investment account and often lower for IRA and 401k accounts. However, some companies may allow for smaller minimum investments if you set up an automatic investment plan or if you invest in a particular type of fund, such as an S&P 500 Index fund or a Total Market Index fund. It's important to check the specific requirements for the fund you're interested in before making an investment. Regarding the initial investment for most funds, $5000 should be enough for 99.9% of all funds.

reference_answer: A 401K (pre-tax or Roth) account or an IRA (Deductible or Roth) account is a retirement account. Traditional IRA and 401(k) accounts allow you to make pre-tax contributions, giving you an immediate tax deduction when you contribute. Roth IRA, Roth 401(k) are funded with after tax money.  Choosing between an IRA and a 401K depends on your personal circumstances and preferences. Here are some key points to consider: * A 401K is typically offered by your employer, while an IRA is an individual retirement account that you set up for yourself. * A 401K may have more limited investment options compared to an IRA, but it may also offer matching contributions from your employer, a free money to you.  * If you expect to be in a lower tax bracket in retirement than you are now, a traditional IRA or 401K may be a better choice, as it allows you to defer taxes until retirement. It's a good idea to start with the 401K offered by your company, especially if they have matching funds. Ultimately, the best choice for you will depend on your individual circumstances, so it's a good idea to consult with a financial advisor or do further research to determine the best option for you.

retrieval_query: My friend wants to put my name down for a house he's buying. What risks would I be taking?
question: My friend wants to put my name down for a house he's buying. What risks would I be taking?
reference_answer: There are several risks you might be taking if your friend puts your name down for a house he's buying.  Firstly, if you are co-signing the mortgage, the risk is that you will owe the bank the principal amount of the mortgage if your friend is unable to pay. You could come out of it a lot poorer and with your credit rating wrecked. Secondly, if you are not on the deed of the house, you would not have any legal rights to the property. This means that your friend could sell the house without your consent and you would still be responsible for the mortgage.  Thirdly, if your friend's house is a second home, he may not qualify for mortgage assistance or relief, increasing the risk for you as a co-signer.    Lastly, anyone considering this approach to talk to a lawyer and be aware of the potential tax implications.

retrieval_query: What approaches are there for pricing a small business?
question: What approaches are there for pricing a small business?
reference_answer: One approach is to determine the lowest amount a seller would accept, which is the liquidation value. This involves calculating the value of the business's assets, such as land, house, furnishings, and accounts payable, minus any liabilities. Another approach is to price the business based on a multiple of its annual earnings. This can be done using a discounted cash flow analysis, where you project the business's earnings out in perpetuity and discount it by the going interest rate. Alternatively, you can use an industry multiplier to multiply the business's EBITDA (Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation, and Amortization) by a factor common in the industry. From the documents, it appears that the 2011 EBITDA multiplier for hospitality industries is 13.8. and in the end for small business in most sectors you can use a rule of thumb, 2x net + FFE.

One of the reason most small businesses fail it is because banks usually know that small businesses are a huge risk and are unwilling to provide loans for them to survive. They aren't able to survive in the short-term no matter how good the prospects are in the long-term. They work crazy long hours and submit themselves to huge financial risk. Most owners have no interest in taking true responsibility for the company's health and in the end business has one imperative: to make money. Moreover some small owners business are lacked of some  intangible qualities of entrepreneurship. They  put in loads of commitment or loads of money into an idea that just isn't right. Or they spend money in the wrong ways.
What does it makes a business to go forward?

A business can move forward successfully by having a solid business model with minimal startup costs and low overhead costs. It's important to have a competitive advantage and offer extra value to customers. This can be achieved by becoming savvy in spotting good deals and reselling products for a higher price. Additionally you need to be careful with the structure, do all the research; understand the risk and opportunities as much you can.  Indeed to move forward in your business you need to make the things happen, you have to do the marketing and sale-link up with your prospective customers. And you have to have a well designed and well operating business. The key to good business management is ""do unto others as you would have them do unto you"" - ie. look at your business from your customers' perspective. In the end the point of a business is to make a profit . However, have some criteria for success or failure. Don't end up caught in the sunk costs fallacy. If the business isn't going to provide a better life than working, pull the plug early.
Speaking about good and bad business, what does it make a good manager?

One of the first things that a good manager must have is empathy. The last thing you want is unhappy employees. You can gain their confidence by being good at your job and making their job feel better. A good manager can find out what people's real skills are then design the role around them. They don't force people into strictly defined roles. It is essential to learn how to do the job and don't be afraid to step in and help out. If you never do this people will assume you think you're too good to do the work they do and they won't respect you or your authority. Being good at something gives you natural authority and people will seek you out for advice/direction. Trust your employees to do their jobs until they prove otherwise. Management is a relationship and relationships are based on trust. A manager should be much more aware of how each person contributes to the whole, what their strengths are, who to talk to about what, and how, and why. Moreover  good managers have the most immediate influence over the comfort of their employees while on the job. Comfortable office furniture, equipment that doesn't suck, amenities to make being at work more of a pleasure - all means of showing employees they're treated as valuable professionals.
How do companies hire their employees?

It depends what kind the company  is looking for hire someone. Sometimes the school that the person attended is a good start. Many companies are looking for skills as marketing, leasing space, setting up a business, and management . Also a good attitude, culture can help . Unfortunately the problem is that most recruiters don't know what they are looking for either. They don't have the background or experience to match someone to a job. Or they ignore transferable skills.
What are the basic benefits that a company to do pay its employee besides salary, of course?

Actually  companies are not required to offer their employees any compensation above paying your salary. However, benefits attract higher quality employees.  Employees want certain jobs because of the tax benefits. Employees expect  the benefits because almost all reputable companies of any significant size offer it. You could run a great company, but if you don't offer a 401k plan, you can scare away good potential employees. It would give a bad impression the same way that not offering health insurance would. Some companies offer better benefits than others. For instance,  Apple offers 15% discount on stock, 25% 401K matching and plus excellent health/vision/dental/etc. benefit. Additionally personnel training  is a great benefit also to the employees.

reference_answer: Apart from employee remuneration, companies may incur various other expenses related to their employees as taxes, benefits and capital. There are several taxes that an employer has to pay  for hiring someone, including social security taxes (which goes to the employee retirement), unemployment insurance tax (the unemployment benefits if they lay off the employee), and workers compensation tax (pays if the workers are injured on the job); Benefits: In the U.S. employers often pay for medical insurance, sometimes for dental, life, or disability. There's usually some sort of retirement plan. They expect to give you some vacation days, holidays, and sick days where they pay you even though you're not working.  Capital: Often the company has to provide you with some sort of equipment, like a computer; furniture, like a chair and desk, etc. Some companies also offer their staff a day care center and that is a considerably large business expense that a lower margin business could no afford.
